comparison.objective: Candidate sets a gripper’s adjustable opening stop, locks the setting, and verifies retention through repeated actuation; PR 2242 exposes and scans a barcode on a sprung training forearm, then restores the scanner and arm.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate tests coaxial driver/wrench seating, bimanual screw counterholding against locknut torque, tool regrasping, and retained mechanical adjustment. PR 2242 tests continuously holding a return-sprung limb while the other hand grasps, triggers, aims, and replaces a scanner, with gentle limb handling.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° opening within tolerance, three repeatable cycles, limited drift, retained nuts, tool removal, and clearance dwell. PR 2242 requires a valid timed barcode read within the scanner envelope, speed-safe forearm motion, scanner replacement, palm-down restoration, and release clearance. Both rubrics provide numeric thresholds; no material comparison detail is missing.
comparison.reason: The shared bimanual stabilization primitive supports different tested abilities: preserving a coupled mechanical adjustment against tightening reaction and proving its retained function is meaningfully different from maintaining a sprung limb orientation while operating an optical instrument and safely restoring the scene.
